body: Grief has no schedule. However today feels for you is allowed to be exactly how it feels.
You lost something that mattered. It makes sense that the world feels different now.
There is no right way to grieve. The way you are doing it is enough.
Some mornings the absence is the first thing you notice. That is not weakness. It is what caring deeply looks like.
Missing them this much is a sign of how much room they took up in your life.
You don't have to be strong today. Getting through the day is already a lot.
Tears can come at odd times, in shops or on buses. Let them come if they need to.
It is fine if you are not ready to sort through their things. The boxes can wait.
Nobody else knows exactly what you lost. Your grief is allowed to be its own size.
Today may be heavy for no clear reason. Heavy days are part of this, not a step backwards.
Being tired is normal right now. Grief is hard work, even when you are sitting still.
If you laughed today and then felt guilty, know that laughing does not mean you have forgotten.
The quiet in the house can be loud. You are allowed to put the radio on just for company.
Anger can be part of loss too. Feeling it does not make you a bad person.
People may say the wrong thing. You are allowed to step away from talk that does not help.
Loss can make simple tasks feel huge. Doing one of them today is plenty.
Whatever you could not say to them still counts. It lives in you, and that is real.
Your appetite may be strange at the moment. A small plate of something plain is enough for now.
Sleep may come and go these weeks. Resting with your eyes closed still gives your body something.
Nothing about this is easy, and you are not doing it wrong.
A song, a smell, a street can bring it all back. Those moments are hard, and they also show what you had.
Saying no to plans is allowed. So is saying yes and leaving early.
Grieving a place, a job, a pet or a future is still grieving. It deserves the same care.
Wanting one more ordinary day with them is one of the most human wishes there is.
Not everything needs to be decided this month. Big choices can wait until you have more breath.
Even on a day when you feel nothing at all, you are still grieving. Numb is allowed too.
Talking to them out loud is fine if it helps. Many people do it quietly.
Remembering can hurt and comfort in the same minute. Both are welcome here.
Time moves oddly after a loss. It is fine if you are not sure what day it is.
A month in, the hurt can still feel new. There is no such thing as late in grief.
Drink a glass of water before anything else today. Your body is carrying a lot.
Open a window for a few minutes. Fresh air will not fix it, but it can make the room kinder.
If it feels possible, step outside for ten minutes. You don't have to walk far.
One message to one person is enough today. Even just the words: thinking of you.
Try to eat something warm today. Soup or toast both count.
Perhaps write down one small memory tonight, only a line. It will keep.
A shower and clean clothes can be today's whole plan. That would be a good plan.
Let someone bring you food if they offer. Accepting help is a way of staying connected.
Put one photo where you can see it, or put one away. Either choice is yours to make.
Small routines hold you up when little else does. Making the bed is one of them.
Consider a short walk at the same time each day. A fixed point can steady a loose week.
Light a lamp early this evening. Dark afternoons are harder when you are missing someone.
Sit somewhere with daylight for a while. Just sitting is doing something.
Tell one person a story about what you lost, if you feel like it. Names are good to say aloud.
Going to bed a little earlier tonight is a kindness you can give yourself.
Make a cup of tea and drink it slowly, all the way to the end. Five quiet minutes are yours.
Keeping one plant, one pet or one corner of the room cared for is steady work. It counts.
When a wave comes today, try putting both feet on the floor and breathing out slowly.
Your steadiness does not need to look like anything. Showing up tired is still showing up.
Pick one small job, like the post or the dishes, and leave the rest. One is enough.
Music can hold what words cannot. Play one song today, sad or not.
Somewhere near you there is a bench, a park or a quiet street. Ten minutes there may help a little.
Ask someone to sit with you, even in silence. Company does not have to mean talking.
Each meal you manage is a small act of looking after yourself in a hard season.
Stretch your arms and shoulders for a minute. Grief settles in the body as well as the mind.
On hard dates, plan one gentle thing ahead. A walk, a meal, a call with someone kind.
Steady does not mean fine. It means you got up, and you did.
Write their name, or the name of what you lost, somewhere today. It is good to see it.
Think of one thing they would have enjoyed about today. You can enjoy it a little for them.
Let yourself rest after any hard task. Forms and phone calls take more than they seem to.
Wash your face with cool water when the day feels thick. It is a small reset, nothing more.
Eating at the table instead of standing up is a quiet way to treat yourself with care.
Halfway through the week is a good time to check in with one friend. A short text will do.
Bring something green or bright into the room if you can. A small change is still a change.
Two months of days like these is a long road. Each one you walked counts.
Look back for a moment. You have carried this for more than nine weeks, one morning after another.
Early on, a single hour felt endless. You have come through many hours since then.
The loss has not become smaller. Your days have slowly made a little more room around it.
Maybe some mornings now start a little softer than they did. Notice that, without pressure.
Things you thought you could not do, you have done. Calls, mornings, empty chairs.
Carrying them with you is different from being stuck. You can move and still remember.
Once, getting dressed was the whole task. See how much more you hold now.
A good hour does not betray what you lost. It sits beside the missing, not on top of it.
Weeks ago you could not picture this far ahead. Here you are.
Hard days will still visit. You know a little more now about how to sit with them.
What you learned from them, or from what you had, is still working in you.
There may be a small plan you feel ready for now. A trip, a meal, a visit. No hurry.
What you felt did not stop when things ended. It is still yours to keep.
By now you know which people can sit with you in this. Keep them near.
Notice one thing that feels slightly lighter than last month. Even slightly is real.
Their place in your story is safe. Nothing that comes next can remove it.
Looking forward does not mean leaving behind. You are allowed to want things again.
Many small steps brought you here: water, windows, walks, messages. They were never small.
In time, some memories may begin to warm more than they sting. Let that happen at its own speed.
This season has asked a great deal of you. You answered it day by day.
Future hard dates will come. You have already met some and stayed standing.
Keep whichever small habits helped. They belong to you now.
Almost three months on, the missing is still here, and so are you.
Trust what you have learned about your own grief. You know its weather better now.
As these messages come to an end, the care in them does not. Carry it forward for yourself.
Tomorrow is the last of these notes. Thank you for letting them sit beside you.
Three months ago this began with a loss. Go gently from here, and keep what you loved close.
